chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-'Amarkki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the speckled crow and the black one, is its eating permissible? He said: The eating of anything from the crows, whether speckled or not, is not permissible.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat crows according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's chain in al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of consuming crows, establishing that the prohibition applies universally to the species regardless of color variation (speckled vs. black). It reflects the Shia juristic consensus on the impurity or general prohibition of carrion-eating birds, distinguishing it from other fowl. The narration underscores the precision of the Imams in defining legal boundaries based on observable physical traits.
